Residues of cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide destroyed using alkaline hydrolysis in the presence of dimethylformamide showed no mutagenicity in vitro.1 An alter- native method, involving refluxing of cyclophosphamide with hydrochloric acid, neutralising, and then reacting with sodium thiosulfate, was effective for the degradation of cyclophospha- mide, but residues from ifosfamide were still highly mutagenic in vitro and this second method should therefore not be used to degrade ifosfamide.
